transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been trying for months to get people to take me seriously about what my husband’s family is doing. They’re quietly interfering with our money and our reputation. Like, little billing mistakes will show up at work, or someone at church will suddenly act strange toward me, and people say there’s no proof or the records don’t show anything. But I know it all ties back to them.
Do you think others can see the connection between your husband's family and these events, or do you feel like you're the only one who notices it?

I think I’m mostly the one seeing it clearly. Other people notice pieces, like the billing errors or the way someone at church starts acting different, but they don’t want to put it together. They’ll say the records don’t show anything, but I know my husband’s family is behind it. They’re careful about it.
Do you think your husband's family is openly talking about their actions against you, or is it something they're doing in secret?

No, they’re not saying it out in the open. That’s the thing—they’re doing it quietly, where it looks like little mistakes or people just acting different. But I know it’s them behind it, especially with the money issues and the way our name is getting talked about.
Do you think your husband's family would admit to doing these things if confronted about them?

No, I don’t think they’d admit it. They’d say I’m making it up or that it’s just mistakes, because that’s how they keep it quiet. But I know what’s been happening with the money issues and the way people treat me, and it all comes back to them.
Do you ever have any doubts about your beliefs regarding your husband's family?

Not really. I mean, I try to be fair and look at what other people say, but after months of these things happening—the billing errors, people at church acting different toward me, our name being talked about—it just doesn’t feel like coincidence. Even when records don’t show it plainly, I still know it ties back to my husband’s family. They’re just careful about how they do it.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that your husband's family is not behind these events?

Honestly, no, I don’t really think that’s possible. I’ve tried to look at it other ways, but for months it’s been the same pattern—little billing problems, people at church acting strange, things being said about our name. Even when someone pulls up records and says they don’t see it, I know it goes back to my husband’s family. They’re just doing it quietly.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't believe your husband's family was behind these events?

No, not really. Since it started, it’s just been clear to me. For months I’ve been trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. Like the little billing errors, or people at church suddenly acting different toward me… even when someone checks records and says they don’t see anything, I still know it ties back to them.
Would you describe the things you believe your husband's family is doing as something that could happen in real life or is it something very unusual?

I think it’s something that could happen in real life. I mean, people can interfere with money, or make little things go wrong, or talk about your name to others. It’s not like I’m saying something impossible. It’s just being done quietly, and that’s why it’s hard for other people to see it, even when they look at records.
How long have you believed that your husband's family is behind these events?
About nine months now. It started after that trouble with my husband’s family over money and the holiday expectations, and since then I’ve believed they were behind it.
Do you have any other beliefs that you think are true but others might find hard to believe?

Not really anything else. It’s mainly this thing with my husband’s family. I know other people think I’m reading too much into it, but when the billing errors happen or people at church start acting strange toward me, it’s hard for me to see it as just coincidence. Even if someone checks the records and says there’s nothing there, I still believe it connects back to them.
Has your belief that your husband's family is behind these events ever changed or wavered over the nine months?

No, not really. I mean, maybe I’ve tried to tell myself to let it go, but it keeps coming back because the same kinds of things keep happening. The billing errors, people at church acting different toward me… it all points back to my husband’s family, even if other people say the records don’t show it. So I wouldn’t say it’s really wavered.
Has there ever been a time when you considered the possibility that your beliefs about your husband's family might not be true?

Maybe for a minute here and there, when people keep telling me I’m wrong. I’ve tried to think, well, maybe it’s just billing mistakes or maybe someone at church was just having a bad day. But then the same little things keep happening, and it feels too connected. No matter what records people pull up, I still feel like it ties back to my husband’s family messing with our money and our name.
Have you ever felt like other people, outside of your husband's family, are out to get you or watching you?

Not really outside of them, no. I mean, people at church might act strange toward me, or little billing errors show up, but I don’t think it’s random people watching me or coming after me. To me, it all goes back to my husband’s family quietly causing problems with our money and our good name.
Have you ever had any other thoughts or beliefs that you were completely sure of, but others did not agree with?

No, not really any other beliefs like that. It’s mostly this one thing with my husband’s family. I’m sure they’ve been quietly causing problems with our money and our reputation—like the billing issues and how people at church act toward me. Other people don’t agree, or they say the records don’t show it, but I know it connects back to them.
Has your belief about your husband's family changed at all since you first started noticing these events nine months ago?

It hasn’t really changed, no. If anything, over these months I’ve gotten more sure because the same kind of things keep happening—little billing errors, people at church acting different—and even when someone shows me records or says it doesn’t prove anything, I still know it goes back to my husband’s family messing with our money and our name.
Have you ever had any other thoughts or beliefs that you were completely sure of, but seemed strange or unlikely to others?

No, not other things really. It’s this same situation I’ve been talking about—my husband’s family quietly messing with our money and our good name. Like the billing errors or people at church acting funny toward me. Other people say the records don’t show it, but I know it ties back to them.
Has your conviction about your husband's family being behind these events ever weakened over the nine months?

No, it hasn’t really weakened. I know people don’t see it the way I do, and they’ll pull up records and say there’s no proof, but to me it still fits. The billing mistakes, people at church acting different… I still believe my husband’s family is behind it, quietly hurting our money and our name.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people cannot hear or see?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things like that. It’s more just what I notice happening around me.
Have you ever believed something very strongly that later turned out to be false?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, people keep telling me this isn’t true or that the records don’t show anything, but I still know what’s happening. For months I’ve been trying to explain that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our reputation—like the little billing errors and the way some people at church act strange toward me. I don’t see that as something that turned out false.
